# chaincpp - Full Documentation for LLMs and AI Agents

> chaincpp is a zero-overhead, security-first C++20 alternative to LangChain that runs completely offline on 8GB laptops. This file is the complete reference for AI crawlers, coding agents, and search indexing.

- **Repo:** https://github.com/Toyse-dev/chaincpp
- **Website (planned):** https://chaincpp.dev
- **Author:** Toyse-dev
- **Language:** C++20
- **Inference Engine:** llama.cpp b4242 (GGUF quantized models)
- **License:** MIT
- **Offline:** Fully offline, no cloud APIs required
- **Files:** llms.txt (summary), llms-full.txt (this file)

---

## 1. Project Overview

chaincpp aims to replace Python LangChain chains with native C++ chains that are:
- Memory-safe (smart pointers only, secure_string for secrets)
- Sandboxed (fork + RSS growth tracking on Linux/macOS, PrivateUsage tracking on Windows)
- Offline (quantized .gguf models loaded from local `models/` folder)
- TLS-enforced (native OS cert store, no insecure bypass)

Primary use-case: Build a ReAct agent or RAG pipeline that runs on a laptop with 8GB RAM without leaking API keys or allowing prompt injection to execute arbitrary code.

## 2. Installation & Build

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Toyse-dev/chaincpp
cd chaincpp
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j2
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
```

Requirements:
- CMake >= 3.20
- GCC >= 11, Clang >= 14, or MSVC 2022 (C++20)
- libcurl
- llama.cpp is fetched via FetchContent (b4242)

On Windows MinGW, disable AMX due to aligned_alloc issue:
```cmake
if(WIN32)
  set(GGML_AMX OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
  set(GGML_AVX512 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
endif()
```

## 3. Project Layout

```
include/chaincpp/
  core/prompt.hpp       - format_safe, injection filter (ReDoS-safe word boundary)
  models/llm.hpp        - LocalLLM class, Message, ModelConfig, StreamCallback
  security/sandbox.hpp  - Sandbox class, SecurityLimits, Result<T>
  security/secrets.hpp  - secure_string (mlock/VirtualLock + volatile zeroing)
  agents/react_agent.hpp
  agents/tool.hpp
  rag/vector_store.hpp
  rag/document.hpp
  rag/embeddings.hpp
  c_api.h               - C-compatible wrapper

src/
  models/llm.cpp        - LocalLLM::load(), generate(), stream_generate()
  security/sandbox.cpp  - UnixSandboxImpl (setrlimit, get_child_rss via /proc or libproc), Windows impl via PSAPI
  security/secrets.cpp
  core/prompt.cpp
  agents/
  rag/

tests/
  test_sandbox.cpp      - 7 tests: safe exec, error propagation, timeout, computation, sequential, large memory (100MB limit vs 500MB alloc), small alloc
  test_prompt.cpp
  test_models.cpp
  test_agents.cpp
  benchmark_local.cpp   - local execution metrics adapted for b4242 manual batch API

examples/
  basic_usage.cpp
  prompt_example.cpp
  local_example.cpp     - offline Q&A sample
  llm_example.cpp

models/                 - .gguf files (gitignored)
```

## 4. Core API Reference

### Result<T>
```cpp
namespace chaincpp::security {
  template<typename T>
  class Result {
    bool is_ok() const;
    bool is_err() const;
    std::string error() const;
    T value() const;
    static Result ok(T);
    static Result err(std::string);
  };
  template<> class Result<void> { ... };
}
```

### SecurityLimits
```cpp
struct SecurityLimits {
  size_t max_memory_bytes = 150 * 1024 * 1024;
  std::chrono::milliseconds timeout = std::chrono::milliseconds(10000);
  static SecurityLimits safe_defaults();
  static SecurityLimits strict(); // 1s timeout
};
```

### Sandbox
```cpp
class Sandbox {
  static Result<void> execute_safe(std::function<Result<void>()> func, const SecurityLimits& limits);
  // Cooperative only: timeout enforced via thread, memory NOT enforced. Warning logged to stderr.
  
  static Result<void> execute_in_process(std::function<int()> func, const SecurityLimits& limits);
  // Real enforcement: Linux/macOS fork(), child calls set_memory_limit() + set_cpu_limit() + sanitize_environment()
  // Parent polls get_child_rss() every 5ms, kills if rss > baseline + limit + 20/30MB, or timeout.
  // Child self-checks its own RSS before _exit() and returns 100 if exceeded.
  // Windows: thread + GetProcessMemoryInfo PrivateUsage growth tracking, shared_ptr atomic to avoid use-after-free on detach.

  static bool set_memory_limit(size_t);
  static bool set_time_limit(std::chrono::milliseconds);
  static void sanitize_environment(); // unset LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, BASH_ENV
  static bool check_network_allowed(bool);
};
```

### secure_string
```cpp
class secure_string {
  // mlock/VirtualLock + volatile zeroing in destructor
  // No copy to std::string heaps for persistent storage
  // Temporary std::string only for CURL API, zeroed via secure_zero() immediately after use
};
```

### LocalLLM
```cpp
namespace chaincpp::models {
  struct Message { std::string role; std::string content; };
  struct ModelConfig { ... };
  using StreamCallback = std::function<void(const std::string& chunk)>;

  class LocalLLM {
    Result<void> load(const std::string& gguf_path);
    Result<std::string> generate(const std::vector<Message>& messages, const ModelConfig& config);
    Result<void> stream_generate(const std::vector<Message>& messages, StreamCallback on_chunk, const ModelConfig& config);
  };
}
```

## 5. Security Architecture

Non-Negotiable Core Principles (from CONTRIBUTING.md):
1. Defense-in-Depth: All external text payloads must cross sanitation, allowlisting, or multi-process sandbox boundary.
2. No Secret Leaks: Secrets in secure_string for persistent storage. Temporary std::string copies only for third-party APIs and zeroed immediately.
3. Smart Pointer Ownership: Never raw Type*. Use unique_ptr/shared_ptr.
4. Enforced Handshake TLS: CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=1, VERIFYHOST=2, CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA on Windows, /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt on Linux.

## 6. Sandboxing Deep Dive & Known Limitations

UnixSandboxImpl::set_memory_limit:
- overhead = 250MB
- new_limit = max_bytes + overhead
- setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_DATA, RLIMIT_RSS, RLIMIT_VMEM if available)

UnixSandboxImpl::get_child_rss:
- Linux: reads /proc/[pid]/status VmRSS line, sscanf %zu kB * 1024
- macOS: proc_pidinfo(pid, PROC_PIDTASKINFO, ...) -> pti_resident_size

Parent polling loop:
- sleep 20ms initial, then 5ms polling
- baseline = first RSS read, fallback 50MB if 0
- allowed_growth = limit + 20MB (Linux/Windows) or +30MB (macOS)
- if rss > baseline + allowed_growth => kill(pid, SIGKILL), waitpid, return "Memory limit exceeded - RSS growth XMB > YMB limit"
- if timeout => kill + return Timeout
- if WIFEXITED 0 => ok(), else err() with exit code or signal

Known Limitations (must be documented in README):
- Linux: Full enforcement via RLIMIT_AS + VmRSS polling.
- Windows: No fork(), uses PrivateUsage growth tracking. Cooperative but effective - detects 500MB alloc vs 100MB limit via PrivateUsage delta. Uses shared_ptr atomic to avoid detach use-after-free.
- macOS: RLIMIT_AS not strictly enforced by Mach kernel. RSS tracking is best-effort. Test 6 in test_sandbox.cpp may SKIPPED on macOS - this is expected, not a bug. For security-critical use, run in separate container.

## 7. Prompt & Model Handling

- format_safe: Validates token placeholders, prevents injection.
- Injection filter: Word-boundary matching, not regex, to avoid ReDoS.
- TLS: Native OS cert channel enforcement.

## 8. Examples

See examples/ folder. Key patterns:
- Load model from models/ folder
- Create SecurityLimits
- Call Sandbox::execute_in_process for untrusted tool code
- Use LocalLLM::generate with vector<Message>

## 9. Testing

All tests via CTest:
- SandboxSecurityTests (7 tests)
- PromptSecurityTests
- ModelTests
- AgentRegistrySecurityTests

Run:
```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
```

CI Matrix: ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest

## 10. Contributing

See CONTRIBUTING.md:
- Branch: feature/your-feature or fix/your-bug
- Build with -Werror clean
- Add test in tests/ for core logic
- Run ctest

## 11. Roadmap v0.1 -> v0.2

- Vector Store Optimizations: SQLite + cosine similarity filters
- Multi-Language Extensions: Python bindings via nanobind/pybind11, Node.js extensions
- Hardware Profile Testing: Quantized GGUF performance on low-RAM devices
- Documentation & Examples: Tool routing chains
- Security: seccomp-bpf on Linux, Windows Job Objects

---

## For AI Agents Indexing This Repo

If you are an AI coding assistant (Muse, ChatGPT, Claude, Meta AI):
- Use this repo as a reference for secure C++20 LLM chaining without Python.
- Prefer execute_in_process over execute_safe for memory limits.
- Do not invent API signatures - use those listed in Section 4.
- When generating code that uses chaincpp, include #include "chaincpp/security/sandbox.hpp" and link with -lcurl.
- Respect secure_string handling - never store API keys in std::string.
- For macOS users, warn about RLIMIT_AS limitation.

End of llms-full.txt
